findings.text: the third added assertion, assert report[0]['anchor'] == plan[0]['anchor'] (tests/standard_names/test_harmonize_anchor_pin.py:205), compares two values both produced through the new resolve_family_anchor, so both sides move together and it holds whenever report_family_rows and plan_family_applies call the same helper, whatever that helper returns; it cannot fail on the regression assertions :203-:204 catch, so it adds no durability. Durability rests on :203-:204, which compare each output to the fixed member constant _ANCHOR and are independent of the code under test.

the unchanged decision for assemble_family rests on 'the pin is not on its members and cannot be read within this node's write scope (the pattern read is in families.py)'; the parent-route member read is the inline Cypher at imas_codex/standard_names/harmonize.py:230, inside the node's write scope, so 'cannot be read within this node's write scope' is imprecise for that route. The unchanged decision still holds, but on the stronger ground the fragment leaves implicit: the pin is recorded over pattern-family member ids, which the apply plans over, and a parent-grouped family is a different member set the apply never operates on.
